script: I saw her stare, then she asked for something I never sold.. I was stocking the cedar boards when an elderly lady sauntered in, probably in her eighties, and immediately asked, "Do you sell walking sticks?" I thought she meant hiking poles, so I said, "Yeah, we do." She shook her head. "No, I mean a proper handmade wooden walking stick." I apologized and explained we don't stock those. She looked genuinely baffled. "Why not? That's so silly. People would buy them. Surely you have them somewhere." I tried again, "We just don't keep them." I thought, our customers are mostly woodworkers; a walking stick is a niche thing. Trying to be helpful, I added, "If you know someone who works with wood, you could pick a piece here and have one made." She stared at me like I'd suggested she build a rocket. "Why would I know someone who makes walking sticks? I don't know anyone who does that." Fair enough. She then saw our shelf of local handmade gifts. "But you have local makers. Why don't they make walking sticks? They're missing a trick." I explained the hobbyists only make bowls, spoons, ornaments—small things, not long poles. Still not enough. "Do you have one of their business cards?" she asked. I said, "I am afraid not. They're not businesses, just hobbyists who bring us items when finished." "Give me one of their phone numbers then. I'll have a word with them." I explained I couldn't share personal contacts. She scoffed. "Then, do you know anywhere that does sell walking sticks?" I suggested online or a local shop that specializes in mobility gear or country goods. She looked unimpressed. "This is all very stupid." She wandered a bit, then headed for the door. Just before leaving, she turned, shrugged at me, and said, "Well, young lady, you've lost a customer today." I wished her a good day as politely as I could. I didn't know what else to do. I answered every question, offered alternatives, explained why we didn't stock what she wanted, protected privacy, and suggested other places. Sometimes in retail people think arguing long enough will make an item magically appear. That's not how it works.
